skill_outcomes.outcome_description: Understand and specify various econometric models including distributed lag, autoregressive, simultaneous equations, discrete choice, panel data, and time series.
Apply estimation techniques such as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Instrumental Variables (IV), Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS), Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE).
Evaluate model fit using goodness-of-fit measures, hypothesis testing, and diagnostic checks.
Analyze time series data using ARIMA, GARCH, and other time series models.
Apply discrete choice models like Logit, Probit, and Multinomial Logit.
Conduct panel data analysis using fixed effects, random effects, and generalized least squares (GLS).
Specify and estimate simultaneous equations models using structural and reduced form equations.
Use R programming language for data manipulation, statistical analysis, and visualization.
Collect and manage economic data from various sources.
Design research studies, collect data, and conduct empirical analysis.
Develop critical thinking skills to interpret econometric results and draw meaningful conclusions.
Work collaboratively in teams to solve complex econometric problems.
Demonstrate ability to learn independently and apply new econometric techniques.
Prepare and deliver presentations on econometric findings and research projects.
